topics.label: Introduction and learning outcomes
topics.groupedBecause: This opening section welcomes the students, connects to previous practicals, and outlines the lecture's learning objectives.

topics.label: Tumour virology and cellular transformation assays
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explain how the study of transforming viruses revealed cellular proto-oncogenes and established laboratory assays to assess oncogenic transformation.

topics.label: Oncogenes, tumour suppressors, and cell cycle checkpoints
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics detail the functional classifications and genetic mechanisms of oncogenes and tumour suppressor genes, using the Rb and p53 pathways as key examples.

topics.label: Mechanisms and consequences of genetic instability
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics examine how distinct defects in DNA repair pathways, replication machinery, and mitotic chromosome segregation produce sequence and chromosomal instability.

topics.label: Multi-step tumorigenesis and hereditary cancer predisposition
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explore how the sequential accumulation of somatic mutations and inherited germline predispositions accelerate tumor progression and malignancy.

topics.label: Lecture conclusion and reading recommendations
topics.groupedBecause: This closing section wraps up the lecture, provides recommended reading material, and previews the next session.
